title: fix(core): the security catalog's metadata-only list keeps every holder of a permission set name, so a named grant is judged by (package, name) in any row order
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DDZYUbJbnXUTqZoZ56k4czR)_
Fixes #32867

Clause-②: yes (widening; narrowing on the agent-account ceiling)
Metadata-protocol: none

Area-lease pilot #33059 · area E2 (ADR-0150 outer ring) · seat `domain:server#5` · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：权限集名字只存在于元数据服务（注册表里没有）时，安全目录的 `list` 以前每个名字只留列表里第一行；现在每个 (包, 名字) 持有者各留一条，按包 id 排序、环境行排最后。
- 为什么改：授权写入点名包时（`permission_set_package`）是拿这份列表比对的，只留第一行导致第二个包的合法授权被拒，而且接受哪个包、拒绝时列出谁，都取决于存储行的读出顺序。
- 风险与回滚：只改 `@objectstack/core` 的一个函数，注册表路径不变；裸名读取仍由存储拒绝两包同名。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts` 的 `list`（`declaredHolders` 一段）与两个新 helper。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run src/security/security-catalog.test.ts`，预期 53 个全过；其中 `[#32867]` 六条。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`createSecurityCatalogReader(...).list('permission')`, for a name the engine registry holds nowhere (the metadata-only path an environment kernel reads its stored sets on), kept one entry per name: the first row the metadata service listed (`declaredByName`). It now keeps one entry per `(package, name)` holder — the shape the registry path already gives — ordered by package id, the environment's own row (no package, or the `sys_metadata` provenance sentinel) last, so the order no longer follows the service's row order.

- A disabled package's row is still not listed, exactly as on the registry path (`servable`).
- A row repeating a `(package, name)` already listed is not a second holder (the first one stays).
- Positions, capabilities, the unscoped by-name registry and every name the registry does hold are untouched.
- A bare-name read (`resolveReference`, `judgeGrantSet` with no package) is unchanged: the store still refuses a name two packages' slots hold, naming both.

FROM → TO (the changeset carries the same rows):

| Case on the metadata-only path | FROM | TO |
|---|---|---|
| grant naming the holder listed second | `409 not-held-by-qualifier` naming only the first-listed holder | resolved to that package's set (the registry path's answer) |
| grant naming the holder listed first | resolved | resolved (unchanged) |
| grant naming a non-holder | `409` naming the first-listed holder | `409` naming every holder, packages in id order, environment last |
| grant naming no package, two package holders | `409 ambiguous-in-environment` naming both | unchanged |
| agent-account grant (or a position binding the name) of a two-holder set, read with no package, only the holder listed second over the agent ceiling | admitted (`setBreaches` judged the first-listed body only) | refused, `invalid_value` at `permission_set` / `position` naming the breach (#32164 fail-closed reads every holder; the registry path's answer) |

Nothing refused on the registry path is admitted here (the card's constraint). The last row is the narrowing: a write the agent ceiling now refuses, that this path used to admit depending on row order.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.test.ts`, describe `[#32867] the list keeps every holder…` (inside the `[#31698]` metadata-slots describe): two packages in both orders; a package-less row first and last; the overlay sentinel row first and last; a disabled package's row (CONTROL: not listed); one holder and a repeated row (CONTROL); a name the registry holds (CONTROL: metadata rows not added).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-package.test.ts`, describe `[#32867] the metadata-only path judges a named grant by (package, name), in either listed order`: four row orders; each holder named resolves its own set; a non-holder is refused with identical candidates in every order; CONTROL naming no package is still the D3 refusal.

## Acceptance notes

- The card's constraint quotes ruling A (a disabled package is still a holder; do not drop disabled holders). The list on both paths has always omitted a disabled package's set (`servable`), and the registry-path list omits it too, so this PR keeps that and pins it; the resolution rule (`resolvePermissionScoped`, `includeDisabledPackages`) is where ruling A is applied, and it is untouched. If the reviewer reads the constraint as asking the list itself to carry disabled holders, that is a change to both paths and belongs to its own card.
- Consumers that now see every holder on this path, all of which already treat the list as one entry per holder: `judgeGrantSet` (plugin-security); the agent-account ceiling's `setBreaches` (`plugin-security/src/agent-account-grant-refusal.ts`, the narrowing row above); the activation door's `?package=` judge and holder count (`runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts`); the activation ledger's holder expansion and `platformPermissionSet` (`core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`); the last-admin guard (`last-admin-guard.ts`); `suggested-audience-bindings` (now proposes per holder); `cleanup-package-permissions` (sees the remaining holder); the explain engine's roster.
- Two package-less rows of one name (no package, and the `sys_metadata` provenance) are one holder, the environment's; the first of them listed is kept. The module doc now says so instead of "an order that does not follow the service's row order" (review N1). Not measured: whether a booted environment kernel's metadata service lists both packages' slots on this path (the card's own "not measured").
